Wait, but in the initial state the head interior was PURPLE (p, 84px). So the head interior color changed from purple to white at some point.

2. After first SPACE: head interior = purple (p, 84px) - block split into purple(top) + white(bottom)
3. After clicking white selector: head interior should become white
4. After SPACE with white selected: head interior = white, block became all white (merged)
So the head interior color DOES match the selected color. Currently white is selected... wait, let me check.
Looking at the image, the white selector (left) has the white underline, meaning white is selected. But earlier I thought purple was selected. Let me check the selectors.
Looking at the ascii image:
- White selector at top: has white underline → white is selected
- Purple selector at top: no underline
So white IS selected. The head interior is white, which matches.
OK so now I understand:
1. The head interior color matches the selected color
2. SPACE paints the block based on the head's interior color
3. When the head is centered, SPACE paints the top half of the block
4. When the head is on the left/right, SPACE doesn't paint (or does something else)
The goal is to make the block match the template: white on top, purple on bottom.
Currently the block is all white. I need to:
1. Select purple (click purple selector)
2. Move head to center (if not already)
3. Press SPACE → this paints the top half purple
But that gives purple on top, white on bottom - the OPPOSITE of the template!
Wait, let me re-read the initial state more carefully:
- Template: white on top (rows 3-7), purple on bottom (rows 8-12)
- Initial block: all white (100px, rows 34-43)
- Initial head interior: purple
After first SPACE (with purple selected, head centered):
- Block became: purple on top (50px, rows 34-38), white on bottom (50px, rows 39-43)
So SPACE with purple selected painted the TOP half purple. This is the OPPOSITE of the template (which has white on top, purple on bottom).
Hmm, so maybe SPACE doesn't paint the top half but rather paints based on the head's position relative to the block?
- Head centered above block → paints top half
- Head on left → paints left half  
- Head on right → paints right half
Or maybe the head's position determines WHICH half gets painted:
- Head centered → paints top half
- Head left → paints bottom half
- Head right → paints right half
Let me test: move head to left, select purple, press SPACE, and see if the BOTTOM half becomes purple.
